title: Clamp two stacked boards with a one-hand bar clamp
instruction: Slide the red bar clamp's lower jaw under the two stacked pine boards, push its sliding jaw down and squeeze until both jaws hold the boards firmly, then let go so the clamp hangs on the boards by itself.
context: Clamping a glue-up is a daily step in carpentry and maker spaces. One hand holds the clamp in place, its fixed jaw under the work, while the other closes the sliding jaw and squeezes, so that the clamp presses the boards together with a real force on its own, and the stack must not shift while it is done.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are centres in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table. Work mat: dark grey rubber, 40 x 46 cm, 3 mm thick, fixed, centred at (0.33, -0.02). Spacers: two walnut blocks, 4 x 10 x 3 cm (10 cm along y), fixed on the mat at (0.285, -0.12) and (0.435, -0.12). Boards: two pine boards, 20 x 10 x 1.8 cm (20 cm along x), 180 g each, stacked face to face with their edges aligned on the spacers, centred at (0.36, -0.12), so their middle 11 cm overhangs a 3 cm gap above the mat. Bar clamp: a red mini one-hand bar clamp, 130 g, standing upright on its foot on the mat with its jaws pointing to the robot's right (-y), its steel bar (2 x 0.8 cm, 11 cm tall) at (0.36, 0.048): a red fixed jaw at the foot, 10.6 cm long and 1.7 cm thick, with a black rubber pad (5 x 2 x 0.5 cm, 20 g) on a spring (40 N per mm, 3 mm of travel) standing 3 mm proud of the jaw's face, the pad's face 1 cm below the bottom board's underside, a red and black handle 10 cm long behind the bar, and a red sliding jaw (30 g, 11 cm long with its collar, 3.2 cm wide, 2 cm thick, black pad) on the bar, its face 6 cm above the fixed jaw's. The sliding jaw rides a one-way ratchet: pushed toward the fixed jaw it moves (about 1 N per 0.1 mm click) and holds, and it never moves back. Trigger: while a finger is within 4 mm of the sliding jaw and the jaw is on the top board, the ratchet drives the jaw on, the bar rises until the pad meets the bottom board, and the clamping force builds by 2 N per control step up to 100 N. The jaw tips start 2.2 cm from the boards' long edge. A yellow and black rubber mallet (39 cm) lies at (0.585, 0.33) along y and a steel speed square (29 x 22 cm) at (0.58, -0.40), both fixed. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Clamping force: the fixed jaw's pad is a spring of 40 N per mm and the force is its compression times 40 N per mm, so a pad that only rests on the stack reads 0 N. Gaps: the least distance from each pad (its two ends and centre) to the board face it grips: the fixed jaw's pad to the bottom board's underside, the sliding jaw to the top board's top. Round the stack: both pad centres 1 cm or more inside the boards' outline, the fixed jaw under the stack, the sliding jaw over it. Gripping: round the stack, both gaps 0.5 mm or less, and a clamping force of 20 N or more. 1.0 (success, held 1 s): gripping, the pads' centre within 3.3 cm of the boards' centre along their length (the middle third), the boards' matching corners within 3 mm, no gripper finger within 1 cm of the clamp, the clamp hanging on the boards (its lowest point 1 mm or more above the mat), and the clamp and both boards still (each moved under 0.5 mm in the last 0.5 s). 0.5: gripping with 20 N or more, but off the middle third, the boards misaligned, still held, resting on the mat or still moving. 0.25: round the stack, but under 20 N or a gap over 0.5 mm. 0 otherwise, and 0 if a board or the clamp falls off the table (centre more than 2 cm below the table top). Real trial: a thin flat force sensor (load cell or force film, 0 to 200 N, 3 mm or less) between the sliding jaw's pad and the top board must read 20 N or more for 1 s after the grippers are clear (20 N is about 6 times the stack's weight and keeps the top board from sliding under a 6 N pull). Feeler gauge 0.5 mm, tape measure and square for the rest.
reset_notes: Stand the clamp back on its foot at its start, open its sliding jaw back to 6 cm (press the ratchet's release), and re-stack the boards on the spacers with their edges aligned.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. Boards and spacers are boxes, the clamp is one rigid body of four boxes, the sliding jaw a box on a prismatic joint, the fixed jaw's pad a box on a spring. Simplified: the bar's flex and the pads' rubber are one spring of 40 N per mm, and the trigger is not modelled: while a finger presses the jaw on the stack the ratchet drives it on (up to 100 N). Meshes drawn only.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (ran to the step limit without finishing). Demo: 1.0 (success at step 327, clamping force 71 N). The same demo with the trigger released after 1 s scores 0.25.
